title: Patton Albertson Miller Group LLC Cuts Holdings in Apple (AAPL)

organizations.name: patton albertson miller group llc cuts holdings

text:
Patton Albertson Miller Group LLC lowered its stake in Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 6.5% during the fourth the company in its most recent Form 13F filing with the SEC. The institutional investor owned 15,504 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 1,073 shares during the quarter. Apple comprises approximately 1.1% of Patton Albertson Miller Group LLC’s investment portfolio, making the stock its 19th biggest holding. Patton Albertson Miller Group LLC’s holdings in Apple were worth $2,624,000 as of its most recent SEC filing.
A number of other institutional investors and hedge funds also recently made changes to their positions in the business. Capital Insight Partners LLC lifted its stake in Apple by 4.9% in the fourth quarter. Capital Insight Partners LLC now owns 6,292 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $1,065,000 after buying an additional 293 shares in the last quarter. Corundum Group Inc. lifted its position in shares of Apple by 15.4% in the third quarter. Corundum Group Inc. now owns 2,242 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $346,000 after purchasing an additional 299 shares in the last quarter. Welch Investments LLC lifted its position in shares of Apple by 18.7% in the third quarter. Welch Investments LLC now owns 1,907 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $294,000 after purchasing an additional 300 shares in the last quarter. Schaper Benz & Wise Investment Counsel Inc. WI lifted its position in shares of Apple by 0.4% in the fourth quarter. Schaper Benz & Wise Investment Counsel Inc. WI now owns 76,786 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $12,994,000 after purchasing an additional 303 shares in the last quarter. Finally, Perennial Advisors LLC lifted its position in shares of Apple by 1.0% in the fourth quarter. Perennial Advisors LLC now owns 31,554 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $5,340,000 after purchasing an additional 303 shares in the last quarter. 58.19% of the stock is currently owned by hedge funds and other institutional investors. A number of brokerages have recently commented on AAPL. BidaskClub raised shares of Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating in a research report on Tuesday. Morgan Stanley reissued an “overweight” rating and issued a $214.00 price objective (up previously from $200.00) on shares of Apple in a research report on Thursday, May 24th. They noted that the move was a valuation call. Zacks Investment Research raised shares of Apple from a “sell” rating to a “hold” rating in a research report on Thursday, May 3rd. ValuEngine raised shares of Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating in a research report on Wednesday, May 2nd. Finally, Morningstar set a $175.00 price objective on shares of Apple and gave the stock a “neutral” rating in a research report on Wednesday, May 2nd. One investment analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, sixteen have assigned a hold rating, thirty-two have issued a buy rating and two have issued a strong buy rating to the company. Apple currently has an average rating of “Buy” and a consensus price target of $205.04. Shares of Apple opened at $188.58 on Tuesday, Marketbeat reports. The stock has a market cap of $956.86 billion, a price-to-earnings ratio of 20.48, a PEG ratio of 1.40 and a beta of 1.26. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80, a quick ratio of 1.37 and a current ratio of 1.46. Apple has a 12-month low of $142.20 and a 12-month high of $190.37.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last announced its quarterly earnings data on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, topping analysts’ consensus estimates of $2.69 by $0.04. The firm had revenue of $61.14 billion for the quarter, compared to the consensus estimate of $60.94 billion. Apple had a net margin of 21.55% and a return on equity of 39.97%. The business’s revenue for the quarter was up 15.6% on a year-over-year basis. During the same period in the prior year, the company posted $2.10 earnings per share. analysts predict that Apple will post 11.43 EPS for the current fiscal year.
The company also recently disclosed a quarterly dividend, which was paid on Thursday, May 17th. Shareholders of record on Monday, May 14th were paid a dividend of $0.73 per share. This represents a $2.92 dividend on an annualized basis and a yield of 1.55%. This is an increase from Apple’s previous quarterly dividend of $0.63. The ex-dividend date of this dividend was Friday, May 11th. Apple’s dividend payout ratio is presently 31.70%.
Apple declared that its board has approved a share repurchase program on Tuesday, May 1st that authorizes the company to repurchase $100.00 billion in shares. This repurchase authorization authorizes the iPhone maker to reacquire up to 11.9% of its shares through open market purchases. Shares repurchase programs are usually a sign that the company’s management believes its shares are undervalued.
In other news, insider Johny Srouji sold 14,976 shares of the stock in a transaction dated Wednesday, May 23rd. The shares were sold at an average price of $187.74, for a total value of $2,811,594.24. Following the completion of the transaction, the insider now owns 73,302 shares of the company’s stock, valued at $13,761,717.48. The transaction was disclosed in a document filed with the Securities & Exchange Commission, which can be accessed through this hyperlink . Also, insider Chris Kondo sold 4,867 shares of the stock in a transaction dated Wednesday, May 16th. The stock was sold at an average price of $187.00, for a total transaction of $910,129.00. Following the completion of the transaction, the insider now directly owns 8,433 shares of the company’s stock, valued at approximately $1,576,971. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Insiders have sold 252,084 shares of company stock worth $44,474,650 over the last quarter. Corporate insiders own 0.06% of the company’s stock.
